**👍 Recommended**

After 12+ hours, I can already see why so many people call *NieR: Automata* a masterpiece.

The combat is incredibly smooth and satisfying, with a perfect mix of fast-paced hack-and-slash action and bullet-hell mechanics. The soundtrack is absolutely phenomenal—every area has music that sticks with you long after you stop playing. The world feels mysterious, and the story keeps dropping just enough clues to make me want to keep going.

The atmosphere is one of the game's biggest strengths. Exploring the ruined cities while listening to the music creates a feeling that's hard to describe. The characters are interesting, and I'm excited to see where their journey goes.

It's not a perfect game. The PC version can still have a few technical quirks, and some side quests are better than others, but none of that has stopped me from enjoying it.

I'm only 12+ hours in, and it already feels like one of those games you'll remember long after the credits roll. Looking forward to seeing the rest of the story.

**9/10 – "Glory to Mankind."**

+ Bombastic cinematic cutscenes and set pieces
+ Weird but intriguing plot and setting
+ Great soundtrack
- Limited and static moveset variety gets repetitive
- Pacing issues due to rerunning levels for more endings
- PC port issues which requires 3rd-party tools to fix

citations.review_text:
wish i could refund that but sadly the game is at least tolerable until like 5h in.
yeah the music is nice, but the game itself is just a side quest simulator, the map is confusing as hell, no path is clear, and for a game that wants to have combat like devil may cry (as in "dont get hit, just combo the enemy"), it does a very boring job of it, alll weapons have like 4 different attacks which get very repetitive.

even on 60% discount, its a waste of 20$

No spoilers ahead.

I got about 6 hours in before throwing my towel in and I can see why this game was not even nominated for 'game of the year' at the game awards in 2017.

This game is an absoulute chore to play and is not nearly as 'deep' as the masses proclaim.  I normally complete the games I start but this is the first one in a while that I've had to wrap up early. 

Positives:

The combat was fun for the boss fights but incredibly dull outside of that (i.e. 95% of the time). The bullet hell aspect is admittedly, enjoyable but the fighst are a bit easy.

The music too is, honestly, not too bad and not a point of criticism.

Finally the graphics and performance are great, no issues here.

The rest however... 

The first segment already seeks to irk the player as it's a 30+ minute long area where one death (when you're still learning the controls) forces you to restart the entire level. A move that does not respect the player's time and should really occur towards the end of a game if implemented, not at the start.

Then there is atrocious level design. Vacuous spaces with orange useless items dotted around in a poor attempt to garnish a very watery soup of platforming ideas.  Innumerable invisible walls and one way paths.  I found myself not wishing to explore or map out any area.

Next up is the poor map and quest marker UI. The quests themselves immediately seemed very fetchy. 'Transfer item to this location and then move back to the original location' and 'move to this marked spot to pick up an item nd then return it'. The main quest line is simply a 'move here' marker. And you'll be very happy it exists because after a few minutes in the first main area, you realise that there is notihing to do.

Moving on, there is the annoying voice acting with characters that don't inspire much pathos. The suggestive outfit becomes a bit of an eyesore very quickly, as does the desaturated palette the game employs. 

After 6 hours, I did not care for their journey in the …

I hate this game. I'm tired of trying to finish it just because everyone keeps saying it's great and how "it makes you question existence" or something.
I don't like the RPG elements. I don't like the music (a lot of it is singing, even when you're just exploring). I don't like the open world (the invisible walls are annoying). I don't like the combat, especially when it turns into a bullet hell while you're still in a 3D environment. I don't like the characters either.
9S is annoying. Every time he speaks, it reminds me of that "The Good Doctor" scene where the guy says, "I am a surgeon!" Except here it's always, "The machines can't feel," or, "Why isn't the government telling us about (blank)?" Maybe the story gets better, idk and I don't care anymore.
The PC port is god-awful. Mods can't fix it. Even if you change the key bindings, the game still uses the default ones for tutorials and whenever it prompts you to press a specific button (in general, it feels like the game doesn't explain how something works or actives. Stopped playing when you supposedly get a scanner and I couldn't figure out how it worked).
If you want a game with somewhat similar themes, play "Signalis" instead.
Navigating the map in this game is so incredibly frustrating that it ruins the fun this game and story would otherwise be...

Been playing for almost 5 hours now and I must say - the game just boring and ugly. The graphics are bad. The world is empty and ugly, so many invisible walls too. The combat is alright I guess, but essentially you just mash. No interesting elements as you play, leveling, weapons, upgrades - all feels just lackluster. The bosses are also more spectacle than interesting and even then not that exciting.

The story seems the only saving grace, but I aint going to endure playing through the game twice (!!!) in order to get to the good parts, and then there are three more endings to go through... A game that is supposed to be a masterpiece, only gets good after 20-30 hours (or whatever it takes) of playing through the game twice? Yeah, sorry but that's just a bad game.

**9/10 – "Glory to Mankind."**

Very beautiful game with an interesting story. Gameplay isn't quite knocking me off my socks, but it's good enough to be somewhat enjoyable.

For context I just finished Stellar Blade and the combat in that game is much more fun than Nier's. Though Nier beats Stellar Blade in almost every other category. 

I'd say Nier is a 9/10. Can't give a 10/10 because:
- The combat is too one dimensional/button mashy and way too easy. I died 11 times on my first playthrough, most of those deaths were trying to go somewhere I wasn't supposed to (big bad boss). This was on the recommended difficulty.
- Manually clicking to loot hundreds of items in the open world, ugh
- Invisible walls. I kind of get it but it still sucks when the environment suggests "there might be something hidden here" and then goes "lol, just kidding, you can't actually go there. suck it."
- Forced Camera perspective in certain areas makes mental mapping a nightmare. It does look cool, but I will have nightmares about navigating the factory
- The game ends REALLY abruptly. I wasn't even aware that I'm already on the finish line, still had side quests open ... boom, credits.
- Menus. The customization is kind of fun but oh my god why does everything take so many clicks. Even just looking at the map is 3 freaking button presses. Sounds petty? Do that for everything
- I don't understand why I have an escort, felt completely pointless outside of the narrative beats. I don't want a friendly AI beating up my already too easy enemies. 
- Similarly I lowkey hate the drone turret mechanic. You just press and hold fire throughout all of combat, And if that wasn't annoying enough, here is a scanner drone module that scans the environment for secrets ... while you hold the other trigger button. So now you get to permanently hold one of your trigger buttons throughout the entire game, yay!

But like I said the combat is fun enough, not too terrible to have fun with. The other issues are some slight annoyanc…

If Steam had a way to review stuff as "average," I would give it to this game. It's not a bad game, but it's not a masterpiece. I think the story with the androids was interesting. I never played the original Nier, so I don't know the backstory of the aliens and stuff.

Anyway, this is quite a weak game by Platinum Games, I can't lie. Bayonetta is a much better hack-and-slash. I don't even know if I should call this game a hack-and-slash, people call it that, but it's more of an action RPG. The gameplay is shallow. There is light and heavy attack, and like 2 combos you can do with them, that's basically it.

Also, the world is really boring as in, there is nothing to do and it doesn't look that good. It's one of the worst aspects of the game.

I really liked most of the side quests. There was this one little robot who begged me not to kill him because he wanted to take care of his animals. Something about that quest clicked with me; it was fun. There was the martial artist android that was pretty fun too, he gets stronger and stronger the more you beat him.

The main story did grab me a couple of times, but it's not that interesting. Also, the music is so good in this game. I would replay this game only for the music, really solid music.

The character designs are good. I like the crow-looking style thing.

Also, death to the Redditors and Steam users. When I tried to search if there is a mod that would cover up 2B because I didn't feel comfortable playing around with her, these "people" have the audacity to say some BS like, "You're misogynist if you download that type of mod," or "UhH wElL tHaTs HoW ThE dEvS mAdE hEr LoOk ThAt WaY, tHe GaMe Is MeAnT tO bE pLaYeD wItH hEr LiKe ThAt." Like, shut up. I hope you never have a happy moment in your life. A good Nier fan is a dead Nier fan.

(Also, I've only beaten it once. I know there are like, idk, 3 or I think 26 endings? Not sure, but I was too lazy to replay it, so I might update the review after I play those ending…

After falling in love with PlatinumGames thanks to the Bayonetta series on Nintendo, I knew I had to give NieR: Automata a chance. I'm glad I did, because it proved that Platinum's incredible action gameplay can be paired with a story that asks surprisingly deep philosophical questions about existence, consciousness, and purpose.

The combat is fast, stylish, and endlessly satisfying, but it's the emotional storytelling and unforgettable soundtrack that elevate the experience into something truly special. Its distinctly East Asian aesthetic and storytelling style might not immediately appeal to everyone, especially players who prefer more traditional Western designs. That's a shame, because overlooking NieR: Automata for that reason means missing one of the most unique and thought provoking games ever made.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features multiple playthroughs where the second run largely repeats the story and events of the first from a different perspective with added context.

citations.review_text:
Quite a lovely piece of art, not the best or most fun video game I've ever played, but it's definitely memorable and well-made.

Pros:
+ Phenomenal soundtrack, every track knocks it out of the park and contextualizes every part of the game world, especially the end credits.
+ Storytelling is given at a good pace, reveals are spread out so as not to overwhelm but kept me intrigued the whole way.
+ Beautiful character moments that stick with you long after the game is over.
+ The scale of some of the setpieces is impressive, it's a very cinematic game that feels like watching a longform anime series.
+ Replayability, but you can't experience the game for the first time ever again. It's impactful.

Cons:
- Platinum has done better hack-n-slash gameplay than this, and there's more running around for fetch quests than I thought there would be.
- The first two playthroughs are essentially the same, for narrative reasons. I was expecting a different ending or maybe a quicker pace, but I was disappointed by that portion.
- It's very VERY gray, not a fan of the color scheme of most of this game.
- Regular enemy variety is lacking. You don't get cool enemies that change the way you play at regular intervals like other Platinum games. The boss fights are cool, though.


I can't give NieR: Automata the "masterpiece" status that others have given it, just because I value "am I having fun right now" in my games more than good storytelling and music. However, it's deserving of high praise for accomplishing what it set out to do and creating a memorable work of art that should be studied and analyzed for years to come (as it already has). 8/10, great game.

damn. just damn.

the first run was baffling because its a lot less than i expected, what with all the hype around this game. fairly typical open world stuff, not always in a great way (navigating the world pre-fast travel was annoying), but the writing is better than most open world games i've played. .......well okay, that's not saying much, but still, i did like the characters, the sidequests could be moving, and Ending A did resonate with me.

the second run was a bit more intriguing. i get why people don't care for having to repeat most of the first part of the story but with 9S, but the new cutscenes provided interesting new context for the story, and (at least on Normal), 9S's hacking trivialized combat enough that i wasn't too bothered by repeating all the boss fights (although i do wish there was more variety in hacking mini-games). there's isn't much new story, of course, but i was fascinated by the slow tonal change from kind-of-corny-but-endearing to something a bit more artsy and bold.

and the third run...i'll say it again: damn. suddenly, everything i understood about the game in the first two playthroughs crumbles and the game starts to use my familiarity with its systems as part of its storytelling. i'd love to go into more detail, but i think people should experience this for themselves. i will say that by the time i got Ending E i was completely won over.

like i think many of the criticisms of the gameplay are fair. combat can feel a bit repetitive and navigating the world can be obnoxious. but at the same time, i think it uses gameplay as a storytelling advice more effectively than other open world games of its kind, and the story itself is emotionally potent to the point of being exhausting. it takes a lot of risks, but i would say they're all justified. 

idk about its relationship to Nietzsche or its philosophical insight, but the way it portrays characters struggling with these big, philosophical questions is raw and engaging. so many ideas …

Funny game about robots.

Great story, absolutely phenomenal soundtrack, but the gameplay got old pretty quickly for me personally. The enemies are all HP walls around halfway into the game, and rather than a character action game it became more of a bullet hell with you chipping their health bit by bit.

The lowest point of the game was when they [spoiler]followed up an amazing boss fight at the end of route A... by making you go through what's basically the same story again except with 9S this time & some added context. Doesn't help that 9S feels clunkier to play, pushing you to spam the hacking minigame.[/spoiler]

But, the story, music, and characters more than made up for the flaws. 8/10 experience.

I love A2!

Oh man what a masterpiece, can't believe how long it was on my backlog and it only made my expectations higher the more I waited, and mostly it matches them. I did play the first one on ps3 way back and while I think the themes felt more fresh back then It did a good job on expand and continuing them, thankfully it has a remake that I would very much recommend playing first. 

my only gripe was 
[spoiler] Having to replay back to back the same route with 9s, I wish there was either more variation on its route or made it so it was like route F (to play it later) or just the cutscenes IDK the first one and Drakengard3 did something similar but it was less of a drag since there were more newer stuff/lore. [/spoiler] 

Regardless, there are no other games like the ones of Yoko Taro, they feel deep without being pretentious, while keeping it fun and exploring the uniqueness of the medium. I know this game is far of obscure but if you liked it, his other games sure are obscure and just as great, but with lower budget.  

I guess I put it off some time because the port wasn't great at launch, but I gladly report that I had only one CTD before changing launch to -dx11 and enabling steam controller overlay, and that fixed it.

NieR: Automata is one of the greatest video games ever made. It blends thrilling, PlatinumGames-crafted combat with a deep philosophical story about consciousness, war, grief, and hope — and every ending adds new layers to the narrative.

The cast — 2B, 9S, A2, Emil, Pascal, Devola and Popola, Pod 042 and Pod 153, and the machine lifeforms Adam and Eve — each play a memorable role, and the soundtrack (City Ruins, Weight of the World) is genre-defining.

Pros
Outstanding multi-perspective story
Fast, stylish combat
Unforgettable soundtrack
Memorable characters
Cons
Some side quests feel repetitive
Story can be confusing if you skip dialogue
Final Verdict: 10/10

More than a game — an emotional, philosophical experience and a must-play for narrative-driven game fans.

I don't understand all the hype about this game: you do the same thing over and over again, no variety of activities, no variety of scenarios. All the side quests are fetch quests that add absolutely nothing to the game

"If you're someone who wants the world to feel inhabited and organically functioning, driven by believable, relatable characters, Automata often comes across as stage props assembled for philosophical sketches."

About sums it up for me.

This kind of storytelling does not resonate with me, making the whole experience feel a bit less than it could've been, both emotionally and thematically. The pieces seem to be there, but the delivery doesn't quite hit home.

The music and flashy combat carried it through. Lots of mindless MMO-style recycled quests actually kinda worked out too, I needed some brain-off gaming.

All in all a good game, I'm kinda sad I didn't get to experience something profound here though.

citations.review_text:
Quite a lovely piece of art, not the best or most fun video game I've ever played, but it's definitely memorable and well-made.

Pros:
+ Phenomenal soundtrack, every track knocks it out of the park and contextualizes every part of the game world, especially the end credits.
+ Storytelling is given at a good pace, reveals are spread out so as not to overwhelm but kept me intrigued the whole way.
+ Beautiful character moments that stick with you long after the game is over.
+ The scale of some of the setpieces is impressive, it's a very cinematic game that feels like watching a longform anime series.
+ Replayability, but you can't experience the game for the first time ever again. It's impactful.

Cons:
- Platinum has done better hack-n-slash gameplay than this, and there's more running around for fetch quests than I thought there would be.
- The first two playthroughs are essentially the same, for narrative reasons. I was expecting a different ending or maybe a quicker pace, but I was disappointed by that portion.
- It's very VERY gray, not a fan of the color scheme of most of this game.
- Regular enemy variety is lacking. You don't get cool enemies that change the way you play at regular intervals like other Platinum games. The boss fights are cool, though.


I can't give NieR: Automata the "masterpiece" status that others have given it, just because I value "am I having fun right now" in my games more than good storytelling and music. However, it's deserving of high praise for accomplishing what it set out to do and creating a memorable work of art that should be studied and analyzed for years to come (as it already has). 8/10, great game.

Pros:

- Great story that isn't afraid to be philosophical 

- Memorable soundtracks

- Fluid combat & animation granting the possibility of comboing with weapon sets

- Good English dub

- If you are only here for the main story. You can achieve the first ending in a few hours

- Cool bosses and bullet hell parts 

- Pascal is such a great character. My man, my clanker

- Pods are nice tools to have. Early game it helped me a lot, but now I barely use them.

- Well optimized. Runs perfectly on my previous build (9th gen i7, 1660ti and 8gb of RAM)

- Diverse environment. Each location has so much charm  



Cons:

- 9s' hacking skills are nice to have but they break the combat immersion. They should have been implemented in a similar way to Pragmata

- Bad character designs. The machines are good but the androids don't fit the setting and vibe. I also find them really uninspired and lame (do not get me started on 2b).

- 9s romantic feelings towards 2b feel forced. I don't mind romantism as long if it serves a narrative and development purpose. But in Nier's case, it only serves the fan service

- The graphics are really bad. Characters & enemies models look good but you should avoid looking at the rest. It unfortunately looks like an alpha build. This game does not deserve to be viewed like this.



Final rating: 7.5/10. A good game but it suffers from a lot of graphic / art direction issues.

Holy smokes, what a game. The story, the characters, the soundtrack (so beautiful), everything comes along together to give you an unforgettable experience. When you finish the first ending the game encourages you to keep playing, and if you are reading this, please do. There is so much more than the first playthrough, and once you reach a certain ending you will get the ability to select Chapters making everything silky smooth (unlike Nier Replicant where you have to play the entire thing all over again).

The bad things are that the graphics seem a bit subpar (countered by strong art direction however) and the game is locked at 60 fps without too many options for image quality. 
Overall I give it a 9.5/10, such an incredible game.

I spent 40 hours in game, completed Route A and and like half of Route B. I played this on a friend's recommendation/request. 
I don't get the appeal. The game's cast consists entirely of Final Fantasy 13 party members I ignored. The shmup portions are stupid distractions. The bosses are mostly uninspired. The entire game looks washed out compared to any other game I play on the same monitor. There are only 12 enemy types in the entire game. 

Combat and character customization is the most fun part about it. Mixing weapon types and utility chips and pods and abilities is fluid and engaging until the NG+ completely ruins that with its stupid hacking minigame. Each time I thought I'd turned a corner and found a new part to enjoy, the game presented a new annoyance. 

At least mods exist to make 2B tastefully thicc. By default she's just skinny anime cheeks on constant display.

What my friend described as a life changing experienced was entirely unspectacular to me. They swore the intro was the worst part. Then they swore the route B part was a drag but that it got better afterwards.

I just ran out of patience waiting to enjoy the game.

I can't even describe how good this game is. I will start by saying if you have not played this, you should play it and avoid all spoilers. As a Yoko Taro game, there are several endings, but only one of them requires you to replay a fair bit of the game, while the rest are a lot more different. I defintely struggled with finishing ending B due to replaying some of the same things but even then there are clear differences between A and B. However, as people say, the real game begins from the end of B al lthe way to the 'true' ending. I won't spoil anything but this stretch of the game is some of the best gaming content I have ever played. As for the ending, it is just insanely well done and my personal favourite ending of any game I've seen. In terms of the game itself, gameplay is amazing, story and lore is second-to-none, and the ost is the greatest video game ost only tied to Nier Replicant. This game has been my favourite game of all time for a few years now, and hopefully you can see why if you decide to play Nier Automata.

As for an Review, it's an Solid 9/10 Game, The story, The Lore, The Characters, The Atmosphere, The Music etc Everything was Great.

The only Nagative for me, i'm still not used to it's credits, Routes, Managing Saves, it was clear drag, i know it can be positives for others, just not for me.

Personal Experience:- It was one hell of an Ride, it was slow journey for me, i completed Route A and B on first few sessions, in Route C i was fed up, dropped it on Jan 2026, picked up again on Aug 2026 after break, completed on one session and it was good choice to pick it up, i liked the ending.

Pascal's character ending broke me, it hit hard, yeah..... No words further.

Thank You To Creators of this Game.

Still 35 Quests left, i might complete it someday for 100% completion, Let me know if it's worth it.

Oh man what a masterpiece, can't believe how long it was on my backlog and it only made my expectations higher the more I waited, and mostly it matches them. I did play the first one on ps3 way back and while I think the themes felt more fresh back then It did a good job on expand and continuing them, thankfully it has a remake that I would very much recommend playing first. 

my only gripe was 
[spoiler] Having to replay back to back the same route with 9s, I wish there was either more variation on its route or made it so it was like route F (to play it later) or just the cutscenes IDK the first one and Drakengard3 did something similar but it was less of a drag since there were more newer stuff/lore. [/spoiler] 

Regardless, there are no other games like the ones of Yoko Taro, they feel deep without being pretentious, while keeping it fun and exploring the uniqueness of the medium. I know this game is far of obscure but if you liked it, his other games sure are obscure and just as great, but with lower budget.  

I guess I put it off some time because the port wasn't great at launch, but I gladly report that I had only one CTD before changing launch to -dx11 and enabling steam controller overlay, and that fixed it.

citations.review_text:
damn. just damn.

the first run was baffling because its a lot less than i expected, what with all the hype around this game. fairly typical open world stuff, not always in a great way (navigating the world pre-fast travel was annoying), but the writing is better than most open world games i've played. .......well okay, that's not saying much, but still, i did like the characters, the sidequests could be moving, and Ending A did resonate with me.

the second run was a bit more intriguing. i get why people don't care for having to repeat most of the first part of the story but with 9S, but the new cutscenes provided interesting new context for the story, and (at least on Normal), 9S's hacking trivialized combat enough that i wasn't too bothered by repeating all the boss fights (although i do wish there was more variety in hacking mini-games). there's isn't much new story, of course, but i was fascinated by the slow tonal change from kind-of-corny-but-endearing to something a bit more artsy and bold.

and the third run...i'll say it again: damn. suddenly, everything i understood about the game in the first two playthroughs crumbles and the game starts to use my familiarity with its systems as part of its storytelling. i'd love to go into more detail, but i think people should experience this for themselves. i will say that by the time i got Ending E i was completely won over.

like i think many of the criticisms of the gameplay are fair. combat can feel a bit repetitive and navigating the world can be obnoxious. but at the same time, i think it uses gameplay as a storytelling advice more effectively than other open world games of its kind, and the story itself is emotionally potent to the point of being exhausting. it takes a lot of risks, but i would say they're all justified. 

idk about its relationship to Nietzsche or its philosophical insight, but the way it portrays characters struggling with these big, philosophical questions is raw and engaging. so many ideas …

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game requires multiple playthroughs to experience the entire story.

citations.review_text:
Nier automata is one of my favorite video games of all time. To be positive, the overall story is amazing, and I love most everything. The combat is pretty simple but (for the most part) quite fun. The lore is amazing too.

For negatives,
The character writing could use some work and a lot of important context and lore is left in random media (plays, novels, mangas, etc). You get a hacking minigame in exchange for a heavy attack at one point, and its horrible and ruins the pace of combat for that section, though its not for the whole game.

But honestly just play it. its great. oh and if you like this buy nier replicant. do it. now.

My personal favourite game ever. Great side quests, main storyline and main cast. The combat is solid and it leaves a large amout of room for different builds and such, though the level scaling can make the gameplay trivial. Though the game requires multiple playthroughs for the entire experience the game shifts perspectives which keeps the game from becoming dry unlike another game in the series.

Overall I would give the game a 9.7 out of 10, though I love the game as a 10, the enemy variety is majorly lacking and could do with some serious improvements.

I hope that Yoko Taro can keep his consistancy with the story and cast in the future, and I hope that Square can improve on the enemy variety and combat in future games. If they ever come out.

[h1]A must play that you might want to avoid[/h1]

It's very hard describe Nier: Automata or give a proper analysis, at least on these short, simple reviews.

The first thing I absolutely must mention, and sorry but it's a spoiler that I'm not going to hide - you need to keep playing after you finish the game. After you finish that, the game truly opens up.

There are many negatives to the experience, some unexcusable. The game's ambiance (which is architecture, texturing work, object rendering) is really [i]really[/i] poor and I constantly thought that this game needs a full remake. Not a remaster, a remake. The game has mind numbing impassable walls that make zero sense too. The engine is crap and needs a lot of tuning. Porting and Square Enix, and I right?

But if you can somewhat ignore that, there's a looooooot to unpack. Way too many little great things like UI modding integrated, and way too many great things like the commentary on war, robotic humanity and many other complex concepts that can't be really covered here. On top of it, the voice acting and music are beyond stellar, probably some of the best ever made. 

NieR: Automata in some ways remind me of some Charlie Kaufman's (I'm Thinking of Ending Things / Synecdoche, New York) movies. They can be a real struggle to watch and digest, but I keep thinking about them years to come. This is one of the main reason I put a "no" as recommendation, it won't move the needle but I think that at least some kind of signaling is warranted. If anything, the futility of it all is worth the playthrough, so please do it.

[hr][/hr]
If you're going to play it, it's absolutely mandatory to play with mods: YorHa Protocol and ReShade. YP fixes and enables a ton of mods and performance issues; and ReShade fixes the stupid fog they added for no reason. The default experience is painful.
